song_title: Concerto for Bassoon, Oboe, and Orchestra in B-flat major, with a graceful allegro
description:
Concerto for Bassoon, Oboe, and Orchestra in B‑flat major — with a graceful allegro by Kay Uwe Rott Two voices rise together — distinct, complementary, deeply alive. The bassoon unfolds with warm, velvet depth — steady, resonant, and full of gentle strength. Beside it, the oboe sings clear and bright, weaving a melody that dances and glows, light as sunlight on water. They move in conversation, answering one another, sharing moments of quiet reflection and joyful, soaring flight. Around them, the orchestra breathes — rich strings, soft winds, and shining brass forming a living landscape, supporting and lifting the soloists ever higher. And in the graceful allegro, the music takes wing: light‑hearted, elegant, and full of life, moving with a natural grace that feels as though it has always belonged. This is not merely music — it is a meeting of souls. Two instruments, one spirit. A celebration of balance, beauty, and the timeless magic of melody.

description:
《龜山》Turtle Island Turtle Island 作曲／林喬｜詩文創作／吳緯婷｜環境聲音、合成器／許雁婷｜ Composition: Chiao Lin｜Poem: Wei-Ting Wu｜Field Recordings, Synthesizer: Yenting Hsu｜ 維繫人心的橋樑 A Bridge that Connects Hearts 最親密也最遙遠，龜山島是所有離人的符號。音樂試圖呈現從外而內進入宜蘭平原的意象，從遠處海洋飄散的微光與霧氣，到土地之上鑼鼓人煙的氣味，在物換星移、不變與恆變之中，龜山仍安靜地在海上與土地平行，守護著。 Sitting at a distance both nearest and farthest from Yilan, Turtle Island is a symbol of all who have traveled away from home. The music leads audiences from without to within the image of Yilan Plain. From the dim light and mist afar at sea to the scents of the hustle and bustle on land, and in the unending stream of eternity and constant changes named time, Turtle Island sits quietly at sea, paralleling the coast, to guard us all.
